text:
Alex: Heads up — seeing a cluster of hosts flapping after the 6.6 kernel rollout in us-west1. p4 instances reporting GPU probe failures and then high host memory churn. Can we triage?
Maria: Which symptoms exactly? OOMs, module unload, or probe errors?
Alex: Mostly probe errors then device-plugin bails. Sample from dmesg on host-42: ```[  123.456789] nvidia: probe of 0000:3b:00.0 failed with error -22
[  123.456790] nvidia: unknown symbol: nvidia_pci_init (maybe symbol lookup)
[  123.456800] nv-host: oom in client 0x1f, killing off some processes``` — then kube evicts pods.
John: Sounds like a symbol mismatch between kernel headers used to build the DKMS module and the running kernel. Did the node image upgrade kernel but not rebuild DKMS?
Alex: Exactly. We have a mix: node images rolled to 6.6 but our AMI still has nvidia 535.68 built against 6.5 headers. DKMS build logs show: ```ERROR: modpost: "nvidia_pci_init" [nvidia.ko] undefined!```
Maria: Any failures from the node bootstrap? systemd-journald earlier showed `dkms build` succeeded on some hosts but not others. Possibly gcc version mismatch or missing kernel-headers for the exact 6.6 patch.
infra-bot: Automatic canary rollout detected: kernel-6.6 -> 30% of us-west1 nodes. Rolling back disabled (manual approval required).
Alex: Autoscaler tried to replace evicted nodes but new instances join in 6.6 and hit same failure. We are losing capacity fast (3 nodes gone in 20m).
John: Short term mitigation: cordon nodes and fallback to older node pool (6.5). Can we drain affected nodes and launch replacements from the stable AMI?
Maria: We have limited remaining nodes in stable AMI in us-west1. If we move traffic to eu-west1/us-east1 we can buy time but increases cross-region latency for some customers. Cost trade-off.
SRE-rotation: Proposed emergency plan: 1) pause kernel rollout, 2) create emergency nodepool with 6.5 AMI, 3) cordon+drain affected nodes, 4) patch DKMS pipeline to ensure kernel-headers exist before DKMS build. Thoughts? :+1:
Alex: Agree. Also need to check firmware mismatch for some P4 machines — I saw a few `nvlink` errors in the same hosts. Might be dual-root cause (kernel ABI + firmware/drv mismatch).
John: Can we hotfix by installing prebuilt nvidia driver binary (not DKMS) on the new 6.6 nodes? That will skip DKMS and symbol issues but we must ensure driver binary supports 6.6. Which driver versions did we validate?
Maria: We only pre-validated 535.86 against 6.5 and a 6.6 internal testbed had a different micro-patch. We didn't test the exact 6.6 packaging the cloud pushed. Risky to push untested driver.
Alex: Reproduced on a staging host by force-upgrading to the cloud 6.6 package. DKMS build failed with missing /lib/modules/6.6.0-rcX-headers. Boot logs show kernel upgrade happened before header packages were available in repo — looks like ordering bug in the image build.
SRE-rotation: I'll pause the rollout and set the canary back to 0% now. infra-bot?
infra-bot: Kernel rollout paused by SRE-rotation at 1778200720. Canary set to 0%.
Maria: Next steps for infra team: - Identify all hosts that pulled 6.6 (query image tag + kernel version) - Move critical production pods to 6.5 nodepool or other region - Rebuild AMI with correct headers + validated driver binary - Add a DKMS verification step in image CI that boots a VM and checks `modprobe nvidia` before publishing
John: Also add a cheap smoke test in our autoscaling path: new nodes run a `nvidia-smi` and `nv-host --health` check before they join scheduler. If check fails, notify and reject the node.
Alex: I can script a quick kubectl job to migrate pods away and spin up the emergency pool. Will need hands on the AMI rebuild.
Maria: I'll own the AMI rebuild and validation. Will coordinate with image-team to ensure kernel-headers and gcc match exactly.
SRE-rotation: Ops note: customers in eu-west1 unaffected. For now re-route non-latency-critical jobs to eu-west1 and mark us-west1 as degraded. Notify support and CS.
John: Estimated impact: 4 p4 nodes out, ~12% capacity loss in us-west1 for heavy-batch workloads. If we fail to reclaim capacity in 2 hours, we should consider temporarily increasing dedicated capacity commitment in another region to avoid customer SLAs breaking (costly, but safer).
Maria: Logging followups: gather `dkms status`, `uname -r`, `lsmod | grep nvidia`, `dmesg | tail -n50` from one of the failed hosts and paste into the incident ticket.
Alex: Pasting short outputs now: ```# uname -r
6.6.0-20260301
# dkms status
nvidia, 535.68: added
# lsmod | grep nvidia
(no nvidia modules loaded)
# dmesg | tail -n20
[ 123.4567] modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia not found in directory /lib/modules/6.6.0-20260301```
SRE-rotation: Good collection. Maria, loop in support with a short internal blurb and suggested customer messaging for degraded us-west1. Use incident channel for updates.
Maria: Will do. I'll start AMI rebuild now and add DKMS preflight. Expect ETA ~90m for validated image, then we can scale up emergency nodepool.
John: After AMI rebuild we should run canary: boot 5 nodes, run `nvidia-smi`, run a small GPU inference job to check KV-cache stability and NCCL handshake. If green, gradually replace remaining bad nodes.
Alex: Thanks all. Posting links to the bootstrap logs in the incident ticket. Will update in 10m with migration plan. :rocket:
